notes.title: 9/2 Patch
notes.content: [p]Happy September! I took the time to get a small patch made today, mainly for that annoying softlock in Tritium Act 2, along with making Meteoric Spin more fun to use.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]When triggering a timestop counter against Ghostwave, Neon should no longer go inside the water blocks. At least, not as easily, if it's still at all possible.[/p][/*][*][p]Doubled the speed of a specific type of flight.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Meteoric Spin has been updated with the following properties:[/u][/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]It now is instantly charged.[/b] You can hold the input to remain airborne, but it can now be used the instant you let go of that input. [/p][/*][*][p]It's slightly faster.[/p][/*][*][p][b]It deals over twice as much damage[/b] and armor damage, and knocks regular enemies high into the air when hitting them on the ground. (This can KO some enemies instantly).[/p][/*][*][p]It is now processed as a break attack (doesn't scale with Resonance, but does more knockback to lower health targets).[/p][/*][*][p]In order to hit a single enemy multiple times, you must switch directions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]It no longer slows down on the ground[/b], unless holding the direction opposite of where you're going.[/p][/*][*][p][b]It can now be instantly stopped[/b] by pressing its input (down + jump) while on the ground, to offer a little more control.[/p][/*][*][p]It can now jump down through thin platforms.[/p][/*][*][p][b]It now works on grind rails. [/b]And it's faster than both the default spin and regular grinding.[/p][/*][*][p][b]You can now dash to instantly switch your direction, even vertically and diagonally. [/b]This opens up a lot of ways to maintain the spin for longer periods if you're actively going for it.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Meteoric Spin is meant to be the perk that offers unhinged levels of speed and traversal, if you can control it. It is much faster than Neon's max speed, but its damage output is less (as running at high speed normally multiplies your damage output so you don't have to combo). It doesn't put you into that high speed run afterwards either, as accessing that run on-demand would break every boss fight in the game.[/p][p]When I initially made the perk, I wanted it to feel like something that could be used to speedrun a good chunk of the game with, but the result seems to be something a lot of people aren't really feeling, myself included. So I said, "screw it" and made it completely deranged compared to what it was before. If you really want to feel unhinged levels of speed at your own peril, now's your chance! It goes without saying that this thing is fundamentally [i]jank[/i], and is intentionally so, so best of luck getting the hang of it![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: 8/14 Fixes Patch
notes.content: [list][*][p][b]UP TO JUMP[/b] no longer triggers Orbital Mirror if you have it activated, and now 100% can't activate Meteoric Spin, even though it shouldn't be possible to begin with.[/p][/*][*][p]Indra no longer softlocks the player in Boss Rush if they died to her second phase before beating her. This glitch occurred in direct response to the fix I made for her fight in this mode during the last patch.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed softlocks in Hexane Act 4 involving the bomb room before getting invincibility, and a bomb room involving hitting a switch through a door.[/p][/*][*][p]Spidrone no longer floats offscreen if spawned in the training room.[/p][/*][*][p]Slowed down rising lava near the end of Hexane Act 3.[/p][/*][*][p]Increased time it takes for doors to close in two-button room in Central District Act 4.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed a fringe-case softlock in Central District Act 3 when falling before the Hazard Eye segment.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue/made it formally possible to kill Hazard Eye in Central District Act 3 with Resonance Breaker.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed red borders from gimmick icons for the board and jet. They were intentionally there but they still looked kind of placeholder.[/p][/*][*][p]Replaced solar shield in Hexane Act 1 with a normal one since it's no longer relevant there.[/p][/*][*][p]Spaced out gears slightly in Origin Seed's final timestop segment.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed textual inconsistencies for "Boss BG Distortion" option, as well as "Clear Nitra/Tritium District Act 4" achievements.[/p][/*][*][p]In fringe cases, charging Resonance Breaker will not allow you to run out of Nodes until the move is performed.[/p][/*][*][p]The miniboss in NItra Act 1 should remain clamped to the arena boundaries, to prevent any rare cases of it flying out.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: 8/1 Fixes Patch
notes.content: [p]Happy August! This one's got a lot of stuff going on at once, so I hope I cover it all here, and that the patch doesn't break anything that I've tried to fix lol. Virtually all of this is in response to player feedback, so thanks![/p][list][*][p][b]UP TO JUMP [/b]is now functions much nicer. It will ignore up as a jump input in at least the following scenarios: Entering doors/warp pads, talking to NPCs, using cannons, using drill, during flight state. [/p][/*][*][p]Dashing [b]straight down[/b] while in the air now makes Neon fall faster. There is still a [i]slight[/i] slowdown at the end of this dash, but it is nowhere near as much as the complete stop it made you do before. I initially made this change max out your fall speed instantly instead of after a couple frames, but it made Neon fall so fast that I'm not sure how easily it'd be kept up with lol. Either way, if the people who requested this change aren't satisfied with the current implementation, I can try it.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dashing in the opposite direction during high speed state now maintains the state, regardless of if it's done on the air or ground.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]After a dash while in high speed state, [b]there is now a 7 frame window in which you can instantly change direction regardless of the direction of the dash[/b], if the dash itself didn't change your direction already. (This means you can dash forward in the air, immediately turn backward and maintain full speed).[/p][/*][*][p]The above two changes mean controlling Neon at high speed should feel far better than it ever has been. Let me know what you think![/p][/*][*][p]Magnetic Platforms in Phospha District have had their snapping range reduced by about 10%. [b]They also now function properly during stopped time, and simply stop moving if time is stopped.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]The rail before the train segment in Hexane Act 1 has an extra boost ring to guarantee the player makes it to the train. That specific rail stopped sending the player high enough and I, for the life of me, can't realize why, compared to other rails in the game. This change guarantees it's not a problem.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Removed[/b] [b]LOAD CONTROLS [/b]option.[/p][/*][*][p][b]When setting inputs, each change you make now automatically saves your settings to the config file.[/b] You can still manually save your input settings to be extra sure. [/p][/*][*][p][i]Addressed[/i] issue (meaning "unsure if fixed but I still tried"), involving player remaining frozen when maxing out during stopped time.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Addressed[/i] issue involving player sometimes freezing in place before doing their counterattack during stopped time and performing the attack after time resumes.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where [b]you'd be abandoned in Indra's first phase area during Boss Rush[/b] if you lost tp her during phase 2.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where [b]Phospha Act 1's miniboss would softlock you[/b] if you destroyed all of its spikes using Invincibility or Resonance Breaker. Resonance Breaker also connects with this boss properly now.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where Phospha Act 3's sawblade miniboss wouldn't properly freeze during stopped time.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated SFX for minibosses in: Phospha Acts 1 & 3, Nitra Act 3.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed boundary break in Nitra Act 4.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where player could clip into geometry if they quickly rose into the air while touching a boss door.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where Phospha Act 1's background would bug out if you somehow skipped the sawblade segment.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced size of sawblades in that segment.[/p][/*][*][p]The "skip area" after Phospha Act 1's sawblade segment now has boost rings.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Addressing[/i] issue where [i]some[/i] players can't talk to NPCs while maxed out. I don't know what causes this, as I've never seen this issue in my life, and some other players haven't either, but the ones who do always experience this. To do this, I made you able to start talking to NPCs while moving, but only slightly. If you experienced this issue before, let me know if you're still experiencing it now, as this one makes no sense to me.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Let me know what you all think of these changes! I couldn't get every problem today, but I've definitely gotten quite a few. I am still aware of some issues, such as a potential softlock involving punching Vaya into the ceiling, and a weird one where the player gets stuck in Tritium District Act 1's miniboss arena despite the two targeted failsafes in place to prevent that. That stuff'll need more figuring out on my part, but I'm indeed aware of them. Thanks again for your feedback and for enjoying the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Hope you all have a good weekend! [/p]

notes.title: 7/27 Patch
notes.content: [p]Thanks for enjoying the game so far! It's wild that we've got over 140 reviews and the extreme majority of them are positive! I'm putting out this second patch to address a couple softlocks and some headache-inducing points that seemed to be consistent for players.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Slightly slowed Neon's fall arc. Once Neon begins falling (while not attacking or in any special states), they will briefly fall slower than they did before, before falling at normal speed. This should help people who feel that Neon falls like a brick, without overhauling Neon's physics nor making the jump feel floaty to those who got used to it. Also, you can hold the jump button to extend that hangtime, which has always been in the game but was never explicitly mentioned.[/p][/*][*][p]Nitra District's Bumper gimmick has been expanded. Instead of a bubble, it now is about as wide as a standard platform. Still looks kinda like a weird bubble though. Neon's attack hitboxes are utterly gigantic, so the actual difficulty of hitting these hasn't gone down that much. It's moreso that the bumper sprites now help players to feel that leniency up front and reduce how much they'd have to adjust to it after the fact.[/p][/*][*][p]Neon will now fall slowly when making contact with this bumper gimmick. This will give everyone a better window to react to it and attack it, without changing how it works. In faster sections, this should give you much more breathing room to prepare for your next few inputs.[/p][/*][*][p]Slightly altered the bumper layouts in Nitra Acts 1, 3 and 4 to account for these changes. Nothing major. It's just to make it so the new sprites don't overlap each other, but they still take up a little more space overall.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a fringe issue where attacking these bumpers would sometimes give very little knockback for Neon. [/p][/*][*][p]Skipping dialogue during Nitra Act 3's cutscene now teleports you to the goal instantly. This fixes a softlock.[/p][/*][*][p]Added an invisible "corrector" behind some of the water zones in Tritium District to help combat odd bounce angle softlocks. There was a failsafe in the game already made for this, but for some reason that failsafe isn't working properly, so I'm adding this second one that absolutely guarantees that if you're stuck in certain zones for longer than a second, the game will automatically force you in a direction that leads out of it. If you find a zone where you're still bouncing infinitely in, it likely means I forgot to put this new corrector there, though I tried to get as many as I could where this issue can happen.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed a gate-related softlock in Phospha Act 4.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issues where Soma's spin and kick attacks stopped dealing damage after parrying the attacks once, even if you could parry the attacks again. While this technically buffs Soma, this also buffs you in that you can trigger timestop right after parrying one of her kicks now.[/p][/*][*][p]Parrying Soma's spin attack now sends her in the horizontal direction you attacked towards.[/p][/*][*][p]The miniboss at the end of Phospha Act 3's orbs now trigger timestop when dashed through.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed crash involving using Resonance Breaker on Blader enemies.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Once again, thank you all for the valuable feedback, and for enjoying the game nonetheless! It feels awesome to make a great game feel even better. Hope you all have a good day![/p]

notes.title: 7/19 Patch
notes.content:
Thank you all for playing the game, enjoying it and leaving your feedback!

I actually typed up these notes once before until my power went out right before sending it, so I'll be retyping these and hoping that the power doesn't troll me a second time. Sorry for the delay! 

These changes primarily serve to address some potentially unfun and unfair "filtering" points in Hexane District, sooner, rather than later, due to it being the "second" area in the game.

[list]
[*] - Reduced hazard count across all Hexane District Acts.
[*] - Increased cooldown of missiles in Hexane Act 1's latter half.
[*] - Lowered total number of missiles fired during the "treadmill" section of Hexane Act 1 right before the train section.
[*] - Deflecting these missiles with attacks now spawns Nodes. 
[*] - Reworked the enemy/hazard placement in the train section and added Boost Rings. This part was overly-disproportionately difficult compared to the rest of the level, moreso than I expected. 
[*] - Added outlines to the bombs to better convey that they can be hit and aren't damaging attacks themselves (meaning that they don't trigger timestop when dodged; same with the missiles, which have similar outlines). 
[*] - Removed all heat zones from Hexane Act 3, as well as the sign warning about them at the start of that level (was understandably easy to miss). They remain in Act 4, with the sign now showing what they are in a clearer area. Those heat zones were understandably less "skill issue" in Act 3 and more just plain annoying.
[*] - The rising lava in Hexane Act 3 rises faster to account for your ability to dash during the whole level now.
[*] - Increased time window for button-powered doors in Hexane Act 4, along with slowing down a couple moving cannons. This partially puts a band-aid on a potential softlock.
[*] - Addressed a fringe-case softlock involving checkpoints in the final battle.
[*] - Warp pads to/from the main hub now show an up arrow above them when usable, consistent with doors in the hub.
[/list]


Once again, thank you all for playing and giving feedback, and I hope you enjoy your weekend!

notes.title: ADVENT NEON NOW OUT! + What to Expect
notes.content: [p]I can't believe my first commercial game's now on the market. Thank you all so much for supporting and believing in me for this over such a long time! [/p][p][/p][p]I know that I should be taking time to let the gravity of this sink in (I haven't been allowed to stop thinking about this game for the better half of a decade), but I first want to detail a "roadmap" so that people's expectations are tapered in regards to post-launch support.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]There are currently only plans for one content update. It will not come immediately, nor will I give an estimated time window for it until I actually get work done on it. (I loved working on this game, but I seriously need a real, actual break.) [b]Remember: there is no dev team. There is no artist, musician, programmer, marketer or legal person that can be contacted for this game other than myself.[/b] This update will, at minimum, fulfill some Kickstarter backer goals that were not added during development. This fact was communicated to them well ahead of time. (Be sure to thank them for their early support, by the way! They were integral to this whole thing even existing. )[/p][/*][*][p][b]This is a full game.[/b] However, there are quite a few things that hit the cutting room floor during development, a lot of which was left in the files. Dataminers are free to have fun looking through that stuff (at the risk of spoilers)! You purchased the game after all; I'm not Denuvo. All of that stuff was moved on from for a reason, but some stuff [i]may[/i] be able to be repurposed for the above update. No promises.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Soundtrack will be releasing on here and Spotify in the coming weeks[/b], just like the demo soundtrack did. Sorry about the wait there! Feel free to upload rips of the soundtrack to YouTube in the meantime, if you enjoy what you're hearing. If anyone strikes you, it won't be me, unless you try to monetize my hard work for yourself.[/p][/*][*][p]Bug fix patches will happen over time if people find important issues that I or my playtesters couldn't. [/p][/*][/list][p]That's all I've got for today. I hope you all enjoy the game, and thank you so much again for your support, or for even reading this![/p]

notes.title: Demo Hotfix - 7/17
notes.content:
[p]NOTE: The full game is releasing in about 12 hours.
[/p][p]I've tried so hard to get this glitch to trigger, but couldn't. But everyone's feedback seems to point to it starting at a point in time where Nyari should use her ultimate attack, but doesn't, specifically when being stunned into a wall, at which point she should normally cancel into that ult. 

It seems that the ult condition kept resetting itself because she was trying to go into the attack, but wasn't being registered as being in the attack, so it kept putting her back in again in a loop. But again, it's super strange how random the odds of this occurring were, as every time I tested, she'd recover from that knockback.[/p][p]
Sorry for the delay. Hopefully this change to the code does indeed fix that issue! And you ideally won't be seeing it in the full game, either![/p]

notes.title: Game and Demo are Steam Deck compatible!

[/p][p][/p][p]The game, both for its demo and the main game, through internal playtesting, run GREAT on Deck with no real issues, to my knowledge. Just boot up the game with no special settings and you should be good to go! Ideally you should see a green Steam Deck Verified status once Valve does their thing![/p][p][/p][p]Oh, and your Steam Cloud will work just fine with it too, so don't worry about your progress not carrying over.[/p][p][/p][p]That's all for today! Thanks for the support![/p]

notes.title: Demo Hotfix 6/16
notes.content:
[p]As the subtitle suggests, the splash art itself is the reason why Steam Input glitched when starting the game, causing a crash. [b]The on-launch splash art has been removed from the game to fix this. You may now boot the game with Steam Input enabled without crashing.[/b][/p][p]
The irony is that the splash art is a fundamental feature/option of Gamemaker as an engine, and is not something I actually programmed, so I still have no idea as to how or why this interaction occurred, let alone the fact that it was possible.[/p][p][/p][p]Either way, apologies for the inconvenience this issue caused! [/p]
